title: Banana Bread
subtitle: Moist loaf cake with very ripe bananas and walnuts
excerpt: A soft, deeply flavoured loaf made with the blackest, most overripe bananas you can find. Dense and moist in the middle, with a cracked golden top and walnuts throughout.

recipe.sourceNotes: Banana bread is an American quick bread that became widespread during the 1930s when baking powder and bicarbonate of soda became staple pantry ingredients and overripe bananas were a common household problem to solve. It appears in American cookbooks from the Depression era as an economical way to use produce that would otherwise be discarded. The recipe requires very ripe, blackened bananas: the starch in the banana converts to sugar as it ripens, and only fully ripe fruit provides the sweetness and intense banana flavour the loaf needs. Under-ripe bananas produce a starchy, astringent loaf. The term banana bread rather than banana cake reflects the dense, moist texture of the loaf compared to a conventional sandwich cake. The loaf became a cultural phenomenon in the UK and elsewhere during 2020 when lockdown conditions meant many households had time to bake and needed to use overripe fruit.

recipeTools.notes: A 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin, greased and lined.

content.text: The riper the bananas, the better the loaf. Bananas should be fully black on the outside for maximum sweetness. If your bananas are not ripe enough, place them unpeeled in a 150 C oven for 15 to 20 minutes until the skins are black and the flesh is soft. The loaf is done when a skewer inserted in the centre comes out with just a few moist crumbs rather than wet batter. The top will crack: that is correct and not a sign of overbaking.

items.preparation: very ripe, blackened; about 300 g peeled weight

content.text: Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin. Mash the bananas thoroughly with a fork until smooth. Whisk in the eggs, oil, sugar, and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt until just combined. Fold in most of the walnuts. Pour into the loaf tin. Scatter the remaining walnuts over the top.

Bake for 55 to 65 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out with just a few moist crumbs. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack. Serve warm or at room temperature, sliced thickly.
